narrative.title: Shared Root of the Wing Access Codes
narrative.scenario: A facility issues door-access codes in families, where every code in a family begins with the same leading segment that routes the request to the right wing. The panel firmware receives a batch of candidate codes and must display their common opening segment for the operator. When the codes share nothing up front, the display simply stays blank.
narrative.outputFormat: The longest string that is a prefix of every string in strs, or "" when no common prefix exists.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters

testCases.explanation: All three codes open with f followed by l; the third character already differs across the batch.
The first characters disagree immediately, so the batch has no shared opening segment.

hintLevels: Level 1: The common prefix of the whole batch equals the common prefix of just two extreme members — the smallest and largest strings in sort order.
Level 2: Sort the batch (or just find min and max); then compare the first and last strings character by character until they diverge.
Level 3: Handle the degenerate cases — a single-string batch returns itself, an empty-string member forces an empty answer, and a full match of the shorter string ends the comparison at its length.
